[
  {
    "id": "pre-fight-overlay-clutter",
    "title": "Qualifier intro buries fighters under stacked chrome",
    "what": "On the QUALIFIER vs HasanAbi pre-fight screens the title, subtitle, flavor-text pill, giant FIGHT button, and STARTING IN n countdown occupy the entire vertical center while the two fighters are pushed into the lower third and partially covered.",
    "why": "The first thing a player sees is wall-of-text UI, not the matchup. On a 390-px-wide phone the characters—the entire fantasy—are secondary to chrome, killing hype before the bout starts.",
    "how": "Collapse flavor text into a single thin line or fade it after 1 s; move the countdown into the FIGHT button itself; raise the fighter pair so their heads sit near the vertical center and the button clears their feet by at least 24 px."
  },
  {
    "id": "twin-stick-dead-zone-and-labels",
    "title": "Stance/Technique sticks lack active wedge feedback",
    "what": "In every in-round shot the two large circular sticks show only a tiny blue/yellow dot; the four cardinal arrows stay dim even when a direction is held, and the STANCE / TECHNIQUE captions sit below the hit targets.",
    "why": "Players cannot tell which discrete direction registered until the move name pops up later. Missed inputs feel like lag, and the first-time tutorial value of the sticks is lost.",
    "how": "Highlight the active 90° wedge and its arrow at 100 % opacity while the opposite wedge drops to 30 %; pulse the center dot on commit; move the STANCE/TECHNIQUE labels inside the outer ring so they are not outside the thumb zone."
  },
  {
    "id": "move-list-cutoff",
    "title": "Techniques sheet truncates the UP list and never shows DOWN",
    "what": "The TECHNIQUES modal (screenshot) ends mid-entry with 'Rising Knee' and a clipped 'Down\ldots' line; no TECHNIQUE DOWN section is visible without scrolling that the sheet does not indicate.",
    "why": "Half the move set is undiscoverable on the first open. Players who open MOVES to learn options leave thinking the kit is smaller than it is.",
    "how": "Make the sheet a full-height scroll with a persistent 'STANCE + TECHNIQUE' legend and a bottom fade + scroll hint; guarantee all four direction groups (Forward/Back/Up/Down) are reachable in one flick."
  },
  {
    "id": "ippon-banner-vs-action",
    "title": "IPPON splash hides the connecting strike",
    "what": "On both the HasanAbi Spinning Back Kick and Asmongold Stepping Lunge Punch ippon frames the huge gold IPPON + name + move-title block is composited dead-center, covering torsos and the actual hit spark/contact point.",
    "why": "The satisfaction of a clean point is the contact itself. Covering it with type turns the money moment into a text card and weakens the 'one clean hit' fantasy the rules screen sells.",
    "how": "Anchor the IPPON stack to the top third (below the score bar) or slide it in from the scorer's side; keep the contact zone clear for 0.4 s before any text lands; scale type down ~20 % on the 390-px baseline."
  },
  {
    "id": "result-screen-score-legibility",
    "title": "Final score 0—2½ is tiny and easy to misread",
    "what": "The HASANABI WINS result screen shows the decisive '0 — 2½' in a thin, mid-size gold face centered under the title; the fractional half-point is especially easy to parse as noise, and the bout record pill beneath it is lower-contrast still.",
    "why": "After a loss the player needs instant clarity on margin. A weak score treatment makes the outcome feel vague and reduces the urge to tap REMATCH.",
    "how": "Set the final score in the largest weight of the display font, at least 48 sp, with the fraction in a tabular-lining face; add a 2-px dark occluder behind it so it survives the warm dojo bloom; keep the REMATCH button exactly where it is."
  }
]
